text:
maria: FYI CI perf harness flagged an unexpected host-side cost increase after the preparse/streaming PR rolled out. p99 latency up ~18%. flamegraph: https://artifacts.redwood/pf/1745555555/flame.svg
perf-bot: rollout ingress/streaming-refactor completed @1745555400 :white_check_mark:
aj: looking at the flamegraph, most time is in preparse_tokenize -> assemble_frames -> writev. can someone paste a pprof top?
maria: pasted top sample: preparse_tokenize_and_coalesce (43%), http2_frame_assemble (18%), writev syscalls (12%), memcpy (9%). stack shows many small-frame paths.
sam: that screams increased syscall frequency. last PR changed fragmentation thresholds (mini-frameization) + serializer variant. maybe frames are smaller but more frequent.
lee: the serializer swap was supposed to reduce copies. odd that memcpy shows up. could be new code path that copies more to meet HTTP/2 padding expectations.
devon: I ran a local stress with a streaming micro-benchmark. avg writev per request jumped 1.2 -> 2.4. reproducer: for i in $(seq 1 10000); do printf "payload:$i" | nc -N localhost 8080; done
irina: also correlating KV cache metrics: around the same time window we see increased prefix churn and lower kv hit rate. more tiny parses -> more ephemeral keys -> lower cache efficiency.
aj: actionable checklist: 1) collect --alloc_space and --alloc_fraction pprof samples 2) enable strace on canary to get syscall counts 3) add internal telemetry for writev calls per request 4) temporarily revert serializer change if needed
maria: opened PR #1312 to roll back serializer as an emergency measure. will gate on canary p99.
lee: I'll add counters in the serializer and frame layer to emit frame_size distribution and writev_count per connection. patching now.
devon: short-term mitigation I'm drafting: in-host coalescer that merges tiny fragments into a small buffer until a threshold (e.g., 8KB) or timeout reached, then single writev. sketch attached in thread.
sam: also consider restoring coalescing heuristics we relaxed last week (min_batch_size=1) which disables opportunistic merging. toggling that back reduced syscall counts in my local tests.
irina: for KV telemetry I'll emit kv_prefix_len and parse_path tags on hits/misses so we can slice by parsing behavior. also recording sample traces mapping request id -> kv keys touched.
aj: owners: lee -> telemetry + frame metrics, devon -> coalescer prototype, irina -> kv telemetry, maria -> canary orchestration + rollback. sam -> run parameterized microbench (vary min_batch_size, frame_threshold) and deliver numbers.
perf-bot: rollback armed by maria @1745555572 :warning:
maria: thanks all. plan to bisect tomorrow 09:00 PT to find the exact commit. will post short blameless incident note and follow-up perf writeup with graphs and mitigations. :coffee:
lee: quick note: if coalescer introduces latency spikes for single-chunk low-latency routes, make it opt-in by route tag (low_latency=true). devon: good call, will default-off for routes flagged low latency.
aj: also keep an eye on TLS write coalescing differences; TLS record boundaries can prevent merging across records. include mTLS path in tests.
maria: agreed. we'll include TLS and gzip variants in the microbench. meeting invite sent for bisect session.
